feedback: For the iron question, accept answers only if they identify that fusing beyond iron absorbs rather than releases energy; redirect 'ran out of fuel' answers to the energy-wall reason.
For sorting, correct any placement of gold/uranium into stellar fusion by noting they require supernovae or neutron-star mergers.
For sequencing, confirm the H→He→C→O→Si→Fe order and note iron as the stopping point.
activities.intendedInsight: Consolidate the chapters of the story — Big Bang light elements, fusion up to iron, supernovae/mergers for the heaviest — and check that the iron limit is understood as an energy reversal, not just exhausted fuel.
learnerActions: Sort elements (e.g. H, He, C, O, Fe, Au) into their birthplaces: Big Bang, stellar fusion, supernova/neutron-star merger.
Put the fusion ladder in order from hydrogen up to iron.
Answer and justify: why can't an ordinary star fuse past iron to release energy, and where do elements heavier than iron come from?
activities.title: Sort, sequence and explain: consolidation check

feedback: If the learner treats the story as assertion, prompt them to name a line of evidence (e.g. the 2017 merger observation) for heavy-element formation.
Encourage the learner to restate the iron energy wall in their own words rather than reciting 'iron is the limit'.
Support production: ask the learner to explain the full chain aloud, since recognising correct statements does not by itself show they can produce the explanation.
activities.intendedInsight: Scientific claims about element origins rest on evidence (binding-energy physics, supernova observations, gravitational-wave detections), and learners can articulate both the story and how we know it.
learnerActions: Discuss with (or role-play) a nuclear astrophysicist the 'you are stardust' story, asking how scientists know the gold in a ring came from an exploding star or a neutron-star collision.
Pose follow-up questions about evidence, such as how the 2017 gravitational-wave observation linked a neutron-star merger to heavy-element formation.
Explain back, in your own words, why iron is the endpoint and how your body's atoms trace to earlier stars.
activities.title: Ask the astrophysicist: how do we know?
